name: Tomačevo Bridge
zag_role: Bridge weigh-in-motion and structural health monitoring
description: Elastomeric bearings at the piers and guided unidirectional pot bearings at the abutments. ZAG, Cestel and Dewesoft Monitoring instrumented the bridge for combined bridge weigh-in-motion and structural health monitoring. A controlled load test in May 2024 ran two pre-weighed calibration trucks over 72 passages across two nights, recording strain, acceleration, temperature and displacement at 500 Hz. During normal operation in March 2023 the system captured a 13-axle vehicle weighing over 200 tonnes.
history: The bridge carries over the Sava north of Ljubljana and is one of the most used routes between the city and its northern suburbs. It is a seven span continuous post tensioned concrete structure of 204 m built in 1982, in two parallel independent decks carrying opposite directions of traffic. The instrumentation combines a Cestel SiWIM bridge weigh in motion system with fourteen triaxial MEMS accelerometers, two strain transducers at main girder mid spans, temperature sensors, displacement transducers and a laser deflection meter, sampling at 500 Hz during controlled testing. For autonomous operation the system can run on two 300 Ah LiFe batteries and four 150 W solar panels.
facts: seven span continuous post tensioned concrete, 204 m, built 1982
500 Hz, node synchronisation about one microsecond
2 x 300 Ah LiFe batteries and 4 x 150 W solar panels (autonomous option)
